questions.question_text: A straight current-carrying wire points vertically upward. Viewed from above, in which direction do its magnetic field lines circle?
questions.option_c: Radially outward
questions.option_d: They do not form circles
questions.explanation: The right-hand thumb rule gives the field direction: thumb upward, curled fingers counter-clockwise when viewed from above.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A current flows east through a horizontal wire. At a point directly north of the wire, the magnetic field points approximately
questions.option_c: downward
questions.option_d: east
questions.explanation: Using the right-hand rule for current east, the field at the north side is upward.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A current-carrying conductor experiences no magnetic force when it is placed
questions.option_b: near either pole of the magnet
questions.option_c: parallel to the magnetic field
questions.option_d: perpendicular to the magnetic field
questions.explanation: The force magnitude is proportional to I L B sin(theta), so it vanishes for parallel current and field.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which change increases the turning effect on a current-carrying coil in a motor, all else equal?
questions.option_c: Turn the coil so its sides are parallel to the axis with no current
questions.option_d: Increase the number of turns
questions.explanation: Motor torque increases with the number of turns, current and magnetic field strength.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: In a simple DC motor, what is the function of the split-ring commutator?
questions.option_a: It reverses coil current every half-turn to keep rotation in the same direction
questions.option_b: It converts electrical energy into chemical energy
questions.option_c: It stops the coil after every half-turn
questions.option_d: It raises the supply frequency to radio frequency
questions.explanation: The split ring reverses current in the rotating coil each half-turn, maintaining torque direction.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: In an electric generator, induced current is produced when
questions.option_a: the coil's resistance is made infinite
questions.option_b: the magnetic flux linked with a coil changes
questions.option_c: a stationary coil remains in an unchanging field
questions.option_d: a coil is disconnected from all changing fields
questions.explanation: Electromagnetic induction occurs when magnetic flux through the circuit changes.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A magnet is moved more rapidly into a coil. Compared with a slower motion, the induced emf is generally
questions.option_c: larger because flux changes more rapidly
questions.option_d: smaller because the coil has less time to respond
questions.explanation: Induced emf magnitude depends on the rate of change of magnetic flux.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A soft-iron core is inserted into a current-carrying solenoid. Why does this strengthen the electromagnet?
questions.option_a: The core removes current from the coil
questions.option_b: Iron changes the current into sound
questions.option_c: The core makes the solenoid's turns disappear
questions.option_d: The core becomes magnetised and concentrates the magnetic field
questions.explanation: Soft iron has high magnetic permeability and is readily magnetised, strengthening the field.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why is soft iron often preferred over steel for a temporary electromagnet?
questions.option_a: It is readily magnetised and largely loses magnetism when current is removed
questions.option_c: It retains nearly all magnetism permanently
questions.option_d: It is a perfect electrical insulator
questions.explanation: Soft iron has low retentivity compared with hard steel and is suitable for switchable magnetic cores.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A compass is placed beside a wire and deflects when current flows. What does this demonstrate?
questions.option_b: Electric current produces a magnetic field
questions.option_c: A compass produces electric current in every wire
questions.option_d: Magnetic field exists only inside iron
questions.explanation: Oersted's observation showed that a current-carrying conductor affects a nearby compass needle.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A domestic appliance has a metal body. What is the main safety role of its earth wire?
questions.option_b: Prevent the fuse from melting during a fault
questions.option_c: Provide a low-resistance path for fault current to earth
questions.option_d: Carry normal current instead of the live wire
questions.explanation: Earthing helps keep the exposed body near earth potential and enables protective devices to disconnect a fault.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Several high-power appliances are switched on together on one household circuit. Which hazard is most directly associated with excessive total current?
questions.option_c: Electrolysis
questions.option_d: Overloading
questions.explanation: Excess load current can overheat wiring and trip a circuit breaker or melt a fuse.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which statement distinguishes overloading from a short circuit?
questions.option_a: Overloading draws excess current through too many loads; a short circuit creates an unintended low-resistance path
questions.option_b: Overloading occurs only in magnets; a short circuit only in batteries
questions.option_c: They are identical and have no electrical difference
questions.option_d: A short circuit always draws less current
questions.explanation: Both can cause excessive current, but their causes differ.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A transformer has 100 turns in its primary and 500 turns in its secondary. With an ideal 20 V AC primary, the secondary voltage is
questions.option_c: 4 V
questions.explanation: For an ideal transformer Vs/Vp = Ns/Np = 5, hence Vs = 100 V.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why does an ordinary transformer not operate continuously on a steady DC supply?
questions.option_a: The secondary coil has no turns
questions.option_c: A steady current produces no continuing change in magnetic flux
questions.option_d: DC has no electric charge
questions.explanation: Transformer action requires changing magnetic flux; after a DC switching transient, steady DC induces no secondary emf.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: An alternating current completes 50 cycles each second. Its frequency is
questions.option_c: 100 Hz
questions.option_d: 50 Hz
questions.explanation: Frequency is the number of cycles per second, so it is 50 Hz.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A current-carrying circular coil is viewed face-on. If its current appears clockwise, which pole does that face act as?
questions.option_c: Both north and south simultaneously
questions.option_d: No magnetic pole
questions.explanation: By the right-hand coil rule, clockwise current as viewed at a face gives a south pole at that face.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A bar magnet is pushed into a coil and then held stationary inside it. When is an induced current present?
questions.option_a: Never, because the source is a permanent magnet
questions.option_b: While the magnet is moving relative to the coil
questions.option_c: Only while it is held stationary
questions.option_d: Both while moving and indefinitely at rest
questions.explanation: Induced current requires changing flux; once the magnet is stationary, the flux is no longer changing.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why is a circuit breaker generally more convenient than a fuse after an overload?
questions.option_a: It removes the need for correct wiring
questions.option_b: It works by converting current into sound
questions.option_c: It can be reset after the fault is corrected
questions.option_d: It increases current safely without limit
questions.explanation: A circuit breaker opens a faulty circuit and can usually be reset, whereas a fuse element must be replaced.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: In a motor, Fleming's left-hand rule relates the directions of
questions.option_a: magnetic field, induced current and motion in a generator only
questions.option_c: light, sound and heat
questions.option_d: magnetic field, current and force
questions.explanation: The left hand gives the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php
